target_customer: AR game studios and app developers needing shared, persistent AR worlds; later teams wanting deployed computer vision models
problem: AR content disappears when a session ends and cannot be shared across devices; later, teams without ML expertise struggled to turn visual data into deployed models.
business_model: Developer API and platform, with custom computer vision proofs of concept
product_category: AR persistence and computer vision platform

founders.name: Mark Stauber
founders.background_notes: Background not found on YC page or TechCrunch.

founders.name: Jaeyong Sung
founders.background_notes: Dealroom and Khosla's job board link the research team to Stanford AI Lab and the Cornell Robot Learning Lab; individual attribution not confirmed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Persistent relocalization and map building that ignores moving objects and builds multiplayer maps live is computer vision and SLAM work, hard for a six person team in 2018.

defensibility.rationale: Mapping and relocalization know-how from robotics research is hard to copy quickly, but platform owners were building similar AR persistence features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No dated source found on incumbent moves; the company was acquired by Roblox in March 2023 rather than displaced, and Roblox said the team would keep advancing its computer vision technology there.

market_need_then: In 2018 AR toolkits were new and game studios such as Happy Giant were building multiplayer AR titles on Jido's API, per TechCrunch. Persistence across sessions and users was a missing layer.

branding.domain_note: jidomaps.com now redirects to Roblox's corporate site, observed in this research.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and practical; YC description stresses a first proof of concept in under a week.

rebrands.why: Later profiles use the shorter name; reason not sourced.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand press, community or merch found; the Maps name no longer fit once the product moved to persistent AR and then general computer vision.

pivots.from: Persistent shared AR worlds API for game studios
pivots.to: Computer vision platform to turn customer data into deployed models (per YC description)
pivots.why: Not stated; sequence inferred from TechCrunch 2018 versus the current YC description.

outcome_analysis: Jido Maps raised a $2.1M seed led by Khosla Ventures after YC W18 and built persistence for shared AR. Its description later shifted to custom computer vision. It was acquired by Roblox in March 2023 with no disclosed price, and the Roblox statement frames it as the team continuing its computer vision work, so it looks like a technology and team acquisition. Reasons for the pivot and terms are not public.
notes: Founding year conflicts (2017 per CB Insights and Dealroom, 2018 per YC). Aggregators put total raised near $2.22M including a roughly $120K accelerator round in March 2018, seen only on aggregators and not recorded. Some profiles mention a 2023 merger; the Wilson Sonsini note says transaction completed 2023-03-15 and the domain redirect to Roblox corroborates. TechCrunch named no competitors and no dated competitor sources were found, so the list is empty. Inactive cause not applicable (status Acquired).
